title: Aboriginal peoples settle Australia
description: Indigenous Australians arrived on the continent at least 50,000 years ago, establishing one of the world's oldest continuous living cultures.

title: First recorded European landing
description: Dutch navigator Willem Janszoon made the first documented European landfall on the Australian coast aboard the Duyfken.

title: James Cook charts the east coast
description: British explorer James Cook charted Australia's eastern coastline and claimed it for Britain, naming it New South Wales.

title: First Fleet arrives at Sydney Cove
description: The British First Fleet established a penal colony at Sydney Cove, beginning permanent European settlement of Australia.

title: Australian gold rushes begin
description: Gold discoveries in New South Wales and Victoria triggered mass immigration and transformed the colonial economy.

title: Federation of Australia
description: Six British colonies united to form the Commonwealth of Australia, creating a single federal nation.

title: Referendum on Aboriginal rights
description: Over 90% of Australians voted to count Indigenous people in the census and allow federal laws for their benefit.

title: National Apology to Stolen Generations
description: Prime Minister Kevin Rudd delivered a formal parliamentary apology to Indigenous Australians removed from their families.

title: Lapita peoples settle Fiji
description: Austronesian-speaking Lapita voyagers settled the Fijian islands, leaving distinctive pottery and founding lasting communities.

title: Abel Tasman sights Fiji
description: Dutch explorer Abel Tasman became the first European to sight the Fijian islands while navigating the region.

title: Chief Cakobau converts to Christianity
description: The powerful chief Cakobau adopted Christianity, accelerating the religion's spread across the Fijian islands.

title: Fiji becomes a British colony
description: Chiefs ceded Fiji to Britain, beginning nearly a century of colonial rule and the later importation of Indian laborers.

title: Indian indentured laborers arrive
description: The first ship of indentured laborers from India arrived to work sugar plantations, reshaping Fiji's population.

title: Fiji gains independence
description: Fiji became an independent nation within the Commonwealth after 96 years of British colonial rule.

title: Fiji's first military coups
description: Two military coups led by Sitiveni Rabuka overthrew the elected government and declared Fiji a republic.

title: Austronesian settlement of the Gilberts
description: Micronesian voyagers settled the Gilbert Islands, developing seafaring societies sustained by fishing and navigation.

title: Islands named after Thomas Gilbert
description: A Russian admiral named the Gilbert Islands after British captain Thomas Gilbert, who sighted them in 1788.

title: British protectorate established
description: Britain declared a protectorate over the Gilbert and Ellice Islands, later forming a unified colony.

title: Battle of Tarawa
description: One of the Pacific War's bloodiest battles was fought on Tarawa atoll between US and Japanese forces.

title: Kiribati gains independence
description: Kiribati became an independent republic, ending British colonial rule over the Gilbert Islands.

title: Kiribati joins the United Nations
description: Kiribati became a full member of the United Nations, strengthening its international voice.

title: Phoenix Islands Protected Area created
description: Kiribati established one of the world's largest marine protected areas, later named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Settlement of the Marshall Islands
description: Micronesian seafarers settled the atolls, mastering stick-chart navigation to traverse the open ocean.

title: Spanish explorers sight the islands
description: Spanish navigator Álvaro de Saavedra recorded European contact with the Marshall Islands in the 16th century.

title: Germany annexes the Marshalls
description: The German Empire established a protectorate over the Marshall Islands for its lucrative copra trade.

title: US captures the islands in WWII
description: American forces seized the Marshall Islands from Japan during fierce Pacific campaigns such as the Battle of Kwajalein.

title: Bikini Atoll nuclear testing begins
description: The US began nuclear weapons testing at Bikini Atoll, displacing islanders and causing lasting contamination.

title: Marshall Islands self-government
description: The Republic of the Marshall Islands adopted its constitution and established self-government.

title: Compact of Free Association
description: The Marshall Islands gained sovereignty under a Compact of Free Association with the United States.

title: Joins the United Nations
description: The Marshall Islands became a full member of the United Nations, affirming its independence.

title: Settlement of the Caroline Islands
description: Austronesian voyagers settled the islands of Micronesia, building seafaring and clan-based societies.

title: Nan Madol stone city flourishes
description: On Pohnpei, the megalithic city of Nan Madol served as the ceremonial seat of the Saudeleur dynasty.

title: Germany purchases the Carolines
description: Germany bought the Caroline Islands from Spain, incorporating them into its Pacific colonial holdings.

title: US Trust Territory administration
description: The islands became part of the US-administered Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands under the United Nations.

title: Federated States constitution adopted
description: Four island states ratified a constitution forming the Federated States of Micronesia.

title: Compact of Free Association
description: Micronesia gained sovereignty in free association with the United States, ending trusteeship rule.

title: Joins the United Nations
description: The Federated States of Micronesia became a full member of the United Nations.

title: Micronesians and Polynesians settle Nauru
description: Seafaring peoples settled the island, organizing into twelve traditional clans reflected in the modern flag.

title: European first contact
description: British captain John Fearn sighted Nauru, naming it Pleasant Island during a voyage through the Pacific.

title: Germany annexes Nauru
description: Nauru was annexed by Germany and incorporated into its Marshall Islands protectorate.

title: Phosphate mining begins
description: Large-scale phosphate extraction began, exploiting rich deposits that would dominate Nauru's economy for a century.

title: Nauru gains independence
description: Nauru became the world's smallest independent republic, taking control of its phosphate resources.

title: Nauru joins the United Nations
description: Nauru became a full member of the United Nations, expanding its diplomatic engagement.

title: Australian offshore detention centre
description: Nauru began hosting an Australian-run offshore processing centre for asylum seekers under the Pacific Solution.

title: Māori settlement of New Zealand
description: Polynesian voyagers arrived in Aotearoa around 1300 CE, establishing the Māori people and their culture.

title: Abel Tasman sights New Zealand
description: Dutch explorer Abel Tasman became the first European to record sighting New Zealand's coast.

title: James Cook charts New Zealand
description: British explorer James Cook circumnavigated and mapped New Zealand, opening it to European contact.

title: Treaty of Waitangi signed
description: Māori chiefs and the British Crown signed the Treaty of Waitangi, New Zealand's founding document.

title: First nation with women's suffrage
description: New Zealand became the first self-governing country to grant women the right to vote in parliamentary elections.

title: New Zealand becomes a Dominion
description: New Zealand attained Dominion status, gaining greater self-government within the British Empire.

title: Full legislative independence
description: New Zealand adopted the Statute of Westminster, achieving full legal autonomy from the British Parliament.

title: Nuclear-free zone declared
description: New Zealand passed legislation making the country a nuclear-free zone, banning nuclear-armed and powered ships.

title: Settlement of Palau
description: Austronesian peoples settled the Palauan archipelago, developing matrilineal clan societies and stone villages.

title: European contact via shipwreck
description: British captain Henry Wilson was shipwrecked on Palau, establishing early sustained contact with Europeans.

title: Germany acquires Palau
description: Germany purchased Palau from Spain along with the rest of the Caroline Islands.

title: Battle of Peleliu
description: US and Japanese forces fought the costly Battle of Peleliu on Palau during the Pacific War.

title: Republic of Palau established
description: Palau adopted the world's first nuclear-free constitution and established its republic government.

title: Palau gains independence
description: Palau became fully sovereign under a Compact of Free Association with the United States and joined the UN.

title: World's first shark sanctuary
description: Palau created the world's first national shark sanctuary, banning commercial shark fishing in its waters.

title: First peoples settle New Guinea
description: Humans settled New Guinea at least 40,000 years ago, forming some of the world's most linguistically diverse societies.

title: Early agriculture at Kuk Swamp
description: Highlanders independently developed agriculture at Kuk Swamp, one of the earliest farming sites on Earth.

title: European sighting of New Guinea
description: Portuguese explorer Jorge de Menezes reached New Guinea, among the first Europeans to do so.

title: Colonial partition of New Guinea
description: Germany and Britain divided eastern New Guinea into protectorates, beginning formal colonial rule.

title: Kokoda Track campaign
description: Allied and Japanese forces fought the grueling Kokoda Track campaign across Papua during World War II.

title: Papua New Guinea independence
description: Papua New Guinea gained independence from Australia, becoming a sovereign Commonwealth nation.

title: Bougainville conflict erupts
description: A secessionist conflict over the Panguna mine broke out on Bougainville, lasting nearly a decade.

title: Lapita settlement of Samoa
description: Lapita voyagers settled the Samoan islands, becoming a cradle of Polynesian culture and navigation.

title: European sighting of Samoa
description: Dutch explorer Jacob Roggeveen became the first European to sight the Samoan islands.

title: Christianity arrives in Samoa
description: Missionary John Williams of the London Missionary Society introduced Christianity, which became central to Samoan life.

title: Samoa partitioned by powers
description: The Tripartite Convention divided Samoa, with Germany taking the western islands and the US taking the east.

title: Black Saturday and the Mau movement
description: New Zealand police fired on a peaceful Mau independence march, killing high chief Tupua Tamasese and others.

title: Samoa gains independence
description: Samoa became the first Pacific island nation to achieve independence in the 20th century.

title: Samoa crosses the date line
description: Samoa shifted west of the International Date Line to align its trading days with Australia and New Zealand.

title: Lapita settlement of the Solomons
description: Austronesian Lapita peoples settled the Solomon Islands, joining earlier Papuan-speaking inhabitants.

title: Spanish explorer Mendaña arrives
description: Álvaro de Mendaña reached the islands and named them the Solomon Islands, hoping for legendary gold.

title: British protectorate established
description: Britain declared a protectorate over the southern Solomon Islands, later expanding its colonial control.

title: Battle of Guadalcanal
description: The pivotal Guadalcanal campaign between Allied and Japanese forces marked a turning point in the Pacific War.

title: Solomon Islands independence
description: The Solomon Islands gained independence from Britain, becoming a sovereign Commonwealth nation.

title: Ethnic tensions and unrest
description: Violent conflict known as 'the Tensions' erupted between rival island groups, destabilizing the nation.

title: Regional Assistance Mission deployed
description: An Australian-led regional mission (RAMSI) arrived to restore order and rebuild state institutions.

title: Lapita settlement of Tonga
description: Lapita voyagers settled Tonga, which became a center of Polynesian society and seafaring power.

title: Tuʻi Tonga maritime empire
description: The Tuʻi Tonga dynasty extended influence across the central Pacific, building monuments like the Haʻamonga ʻa Maui.

title: Dutch explorers reach Tonga
description: Dutch navigators Schouten and Le Maire became the first Europeans to make contact with Tonga.

title: Tāufaʻāhau unites Tonga
description: King George Tupou I unified the islands and founded the modern Tongan monarchy.

title: Tonga adopts a constitution
description: King George Tupou I promulgated a constitution, establishing Tonga as a constitutional monarchy.

title: Treaty of Friendship with Britain
description: Tonga became a British protected state while retaining its monarchy and never being formally colonized.

title: Tonga regains full sovereignty
description: Tonga ended its protected status with Britain and became a fully independent member of the Commonwealth.

title: Democratic reforms enacted
description: Tonga held elections under reforms that gave commoners majority control of parliament for the first time.

title: Polynesian settlement of Tuvalu
description: Polynesian voyagers settled the atolls of Tuvalu, sustaining communities through fishing and navigation.

title: European sighting by Mendaña
description: Spanish explorer Álvaro de Mendaña sighted Nui, the first recorded European contact with Tuvalu.

title: British protectorate over the Ellice Islands
description: The Ellice Islands became part of a British protectorate, later joined with the Gilbert Islands as a colony.

title: Ellice Islanders vote to separate
description: A referendum saw the Polynesian Ellice Islands vote to separate from the Micronesian Gilbert Islands.

title: Tuvalu gains independence
description: Tuvalu became an independent nation within the Commonwealth, adopting its own name and flag.

title: Tuvalu joins the United Nations
description: Tuvalu became a UN member, partly funded by leasing its '.tv' internet domain name.

title: Climate advocacy on the world stage
description: Tuvalu's foreign minister addressed COP26 standing knee-deep in seawater to highlight rising sea levels.

title: Lapita settlement of Vanuatu
description: Lapita voyagers settled the islands of Vanuatu, leaving behind some of the Pacific's richest archaeological sites.

title: Quirós reaches Espiritu Santo
description: Portuguese explorer Pedro Fernandes de Queirós landed on Espiritu Santo, the first European in Vanuatu.

title: Cook names the New Hebrides
description: British explorer James Cook charted the islands and named the archipelago the New Hebrides.

title: Anglo-French Condominium
description: Britain and France established a joint colonial administration over the New Hebrides, a unique shared rule.

title: Vanuatu gains independence
description: The New Hebrides became the independent Republic of Vanuatu, ending Anglo-French colonial rule.

title: Vanuatu joins the United Nations
description: Vanuatu became a full member of the United Nations, affirming its place among sovereign states.

title: Cyclone Pam devastates Vanuatu
description: Cyclone Pam, one of the strongest storms in Pacific history, caused widespread destruction across Vanuatu.
